edges.mechanism: Chamomile may potentiate warfarin (proposed coumarin-like constituents and CYP inhibition); case of multiple internal hemorrhages with chamomile tea/lotion during warfarin therapy. Chamomile alone did not change PT/INR in volunteers not on warfarin.
edges.evidence: Case report plus systematic reviews rating chamomile as major-severity/bleeding-risk herb; volunteer RCT negative for chamomile alone; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: INR may rise when chamomile is added to warfarin; chamomile alone does not prolong PT/INR/aPTT.
edges.evidence: Case report and crossover RCT in healthy volunteers (n=12)

edges.mechanism: Apigenin competitively inhibits CYP2C9 (IC50 ~4-10 uM in human liver microsomes/recombinant enzyme) and shows mixed-type inhibition; dietary plasma levels are sub-micromolar.
edges.evidence: In vitro only; no human PK study

edges.mechanism: Apigenin reversibly inhibits CYP3A4 in vitro; crude chamomile extract inhibits CYP3A4 in vitro; chamomile extract induced hepatic Cyp3a in mice, so net direction in humans is uncertain.
edges.evidence: In vitro and rodent data only

edges.mechanism: Sirolimus is a narrow-therapeutic-index CYP3A4/P-gp substrate; apigenin inhibits CYP3A4 in vitro and increased exposure to CYP3A/P-gp/BCRP substrates (dasatinib, paclitaxel) in rats. Extrapolated, not studied with rapamycin.
edges.evidence: Mechanistic extrapolation from in vitro and rat PK studies; no human data

edges.mechanism: Apigenin pretreatment (40 mg/kg) markedly increased dasatinib Cmax/AUC and half-life in rats via modulation of CYP3A2, P-gp and BCRP.
edges.evidence: Rat PK study

edges.mechanism: Apigenin increased oral paclitaxel AUC and Cmax dose-dependently in rats via P-gp inhibition. A human chamomile oral-solution RCT during paclitaxel reported no AEs (PK not measured).
edges.evidence: Rat PK study; human RCT without PK

edges.mechanism: Apigenin (250 mg/kg) increased venlafaxine AUC by 40.9% in rats and inhibited its metabolism in human liver microsomes (IC50 58 uM).
edges.evidence: Rat PK and in vitro; dose far above human intake

edges.mechanism: Apigenin binds the benzodiazepine site and enhanced diazepam's positive modulation of GABA-A receptors in vitro; drowsiness is a common chamomile AE; NCCIH lists sedatives as a theoretical interaction.
edges.evidence: In vitro/animal plus AE review; no clinical interaction study

edges.mechanism: Melatonin 6-hydroxylation is mainly CYP1A2; apigenin and chamomile oil constituents inhibit CYP1A2 in vitro, so melatonin levels and sedation could rise.
edges.evidence: Mechanistic only

edges.mechanism: Apigenin antagonizes TxA2 receptors and potentiated aspirin's inhibition of arachidonic-acid-induced aggregation ex vivo; dietary apigenin 84 mg/d had no in vivo platelet effect.
edges.evidence: Ex vivo/in vitro; human dietary crossover negative

edges.mechanism: Chamomile tea (3 g three times daily, 8 wk) lowered HbA1c, insulin and HOMA-IR in T2DM; additive glucose lowering possible.
edges.evidence: Single-blind RCT (n=64); very low certainty

edges.mechanism: NCCIH cites preliminary studies that chamomile may decrease the effect of birth control pills; mechanism unclear (possible estrogen-like activity).
edges.evidence: Agency fact sheet citing preliminary data

edges.mechanism: Apigenin is a partial ER agonist in mice and an aromatase inhibitor in vitro; no in vivo aromatase or uterotrophic effect at 50 mg/kg in rats. NCCIH cautions chamomile might worsen estrogen-sensitive conditions.
edges.evidence: Preclinical plus agency caution; no human data

edges.mechanism: Apigenin acts as a mixed progesterone-receptor agonist and blocked genistein-stimulated uterine epithelial proliferation in mice.
edges.evidence: Single animal/in vitro study

edges.mechanism: Apigenin inhibits the NADase CD38; apigenin and NR each raised brain NAD+ and suppressed neuroinflammation in mice. Combination untested in humans.
edges.evidence: Mechanistic/preclinical only

edges.mechanism: CD38 is the main enzyme degrading NMN in vivo and drives age-related NAD+ decline; apigenin inhibits CD38 and raised NAD+ in obese mice. Combination untested in humans.
edges.evidence: Mechanistic/preclinical only

edges.mechanism: Both quercetin and apigenin inhibit CD38 and raise cellular NAD+; additive effect is hypothetical.
edges.evidence: In vitro/mouse only

edges.mechanism: Apigenin + magnesium prolonged sleep more than either alone in mice; a 2-week human RCT of apigenin 50 mg + magnesium L-threonate + L-theanine showed no benefit over placebo.
edges.evidence: Mouse study; null human RCT of the stack

edges.mechanism: Chamomile tea taken with a meal reduced non-heme iron absorption by 47% (polyphenol binding).
edges.evidence: Human isotope absorption study

edges.mechanism: Type I hypersensitivity including anaphylaxis to chamomile; cross-reactivity with mugwort, birch pollen (Bet v 1 homologue) and celery.
edges.evidence: Case series, SR of AEs (3 anaphylaxis case reports), NCCIH

edges.mechanism: Insufficient safety data for chamomile/apigenin supplements in pregnancy and lactation.
edges.evidence: Systematic reviews; evidence too weak for recommendations
